expected_level_description: You can: - explain how products and services are delivered through different methodologies - follow an appropriate approach to complete your work within the delivery methodology used by your team - adapt how you work and the work you produce based on your team's delivery methodology to ensure you deliver value - adapt how you work with other roles in a multidisciplinary team in line with the delivery methodology

You can: - work with others to ensure appropriate test coverage, data and scenarios, in line with acceptance criteria - document and triage defects, and their risks, so they can be traced and resolved - work with others to review test outcomes to validate that business and user needs are met

You can: - select appropriate business modelling techniques to support analysis, decision making and stakeholder understanding - elicit appropriate information to create effective business models - create models and diagrams that represent the organisation, processes, relationships, information and interactions - use existing and new models to ensure alignment to the organisation’s goals

You can: - analyse and evaluate business processes to identify problems and opportunities - design, prioritise and facilitate the implementation of business process improvements, with some support - validate improvements to business processes through testing

You can: - assess how proposed changes affect roles, processes, policies, data, systems and customer or user experience - support the definition of measurable outcomes, measures and indicators - work with the business and other professions to support business readiness

You can: - plan and use the most appropriate analysis techniques to understand the context, the problem and root causes - communicate how your work supports and aligns to strategic contexts and goals - define problem statements and develop and evaluate multiple options - formulate recommendations, considering feasibility, benefits and impact

skill: Defining and managing business needs, user needs and requirements
expected_level_description: You can: - elicit, analyse, challenge and validate business and user needs, addressing conflicts - define artefacts, such as problem statements, epics, features, user stories, acceptance criteria and non-functional requirements, to communicate business and user needs - manage artefacts and ensure traceability in line with a defined approach - facilitate the prioritisation of needs with minimal supervision

You can: - identify and analyse the functionality that systems deliver or need to deliver - create system and data models and documentation with minimal supervision - work with others in a multidisciplinary team to identify gaps in functionality and user experience, and their impact

You can: - identify important stakeholders and communicate with them clearly and regularly - tailor communication to stakeholders' needs and work with them to build relationships while meeting user needs - build and reach consensus with stakeholders - work to improve stakeholder relationships using evidence to explain decisions

You can: - contribute to the analysis of user journeys and interactions - use available quantitative and qualitative evidence to identify pain points for users - identify where additional evidence is needed to understand user experience - communicate how identified issues affect users and service outcomes

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - read and use FHIR resources, profiles, and APIs - build or test simple integrations under guidance - check messages against a specification
You can: - explain the difference between a clinical terminology and a classification - recognise common terminologies such as SNOMED CT and ICD
